**Telegram Notification**
- Updated message for this occurrence to Ethereum Protocol Updates channel
I would be happy to present the case for 2x shorter slot times as a Glamsterdam headliner feature: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-7782-the-case-for-2x-shorter-slot-times-in-glamsterdam/24616
I'd like to bring up the topic of BPOs and what our rollout strategy is going to be.

I won't be able to attend this week's call (traveling) but I would like to bring up the following:

* https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4393
  * Proposed by Agnish. We want to remove peer sampling from the specs & keep custody sampling. I believe this is a good change that would simplify the specs. Before merging this, I want confirmation that client teams want this.
* https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4394
  * Proposed by Manu. I'm unsure how other client teams feel about it.
* https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4406
  * There was some confusion about (1) when the `nfd` entry should be added to the ENR and (2) whether or not some `eth2` entry values should change too. I'd like to request reviews from clients to ensure this is clear now.
* https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4407
  * Kasey raised a concern around peering behavior when `nfd` (next fork digest) values are different. The specs stated that nodes MUST disconnect from peers with differing views at the fork. On discord, many of us agreed that this requirement is a bit too strong and that MAY disconnect would be more appropriate. Also, this PR explicitly states that peers MUST NOT disconnect prior to the fork. I'd like to request reviews from clients.
* https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3510
  * This PR defines explicit slot operation deadlines in milliseconds. This promotes a flexible time-setting scheme and eliminates the legacy technical debt around `INTERVALS_PER_SLOT`. Personally, I want to include this in the upcoming release, but we need buy-in from clients first. Somewhat related: if merged, I will follow up with another PR which adds a new `SLOT_TIME_MS` preset (and keeps the original `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` config for now).

Hi can we add a discussion on Jimmy Chen's post on shipping PeerDAS in 2025 in the [SigmaPrime blog here](https://blog.sigmaprime.io/shipping-peerdas.html)

It would be ideal for CL teams to be able to respond to the three key questions in this post. 
1. Can we freeze the spec today? If not, what's missing?
2. How much scaling can we safely ship in Fusaka and subsequent BPO forks? Even if it's below PeerDAS's theoretical limit (72 blobs), it still delivers value.
3. What must be done before shipping this version? What improvements can wait until after the fork or the next fork?

We can't freeze the spec today because it's still maturing. However, I think the focus should be on maturing the current PeerDAS feature set with a high focus on performance testing. My suggestion regarding the BPO forks on the mainnet is to decide on it later, once there is significantly more performance testing data, including data from testnets.
